full_text_en:
Gao Qingting and Liu Guiliang — Smuggling and Conniving at Smuggling Case

Defendant: Gao Qingting, male, 48 years old, native of Jinan City, Shandong Province, former Deputy Commissioner of Jinan Customs. Arrested on January 14, 1997.

Defense Counsel: Wang Guangren and Li Shuguang, lawyers of Jinan Zhongcheng Law Firm.

Defendant: Liu Guiliang, male, 36 years old, native of Wulian County, Shandong Province, former Deputy Section Chief of the Investigation Division of Jinan Customs. Arrested on January 14, 1997.

Defense Counsel: Ye Shougang, lawyer of Jinan Luozhong Law Firm.

Defense Counsel: Hao Chunsen, lawyer of Shandong Wenhan Law Firm.

The People's Procuratorate of Jinan, Shandong Province instituted a public prosecution before the Jinan Intermediate People's Court, charging Defendant Gao Qingting with the crime of smuggling ordinary articles and Defendant Liu Guiliang with the crime of conniving at smuggling.

The indictment alleged: Defendant Gao Qingting, in collusion with others, smuggled goods valued at over RMB 21 million and evaded customs duties of over RMB 3.7 million, constituting the crime of smuggling ordinary articles. Defendant Liu Guiliang, clearly knowing the goods were smuggled, still released them, constituting the crime of conniving at smuggling. A lawful punishment was requested.

Defendant Gao Qingting and his defense counsel argued: Gao Qingting did not participate in smuggling, but merely connived at smuggling, and requested a fair disposition.

The defense counsel for Defendant Liu Guiliang argued: Liu Guiliang's actions were carried out under the direction of Gao Qingting, and his attitude of admitting guilt was good, requesting a lighter punishment.

The Jinan Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found the following facts:

In the summer of 1994, Defendant Gao Qingting was introduced to Li Yongjian (at large), General Manager of Hong Kong Dasheng Trading Company, and thereafter the two socialized frequently.

In the spring of 1996, Li Yongjian, intending to cooperate with Jinan Hengdeli Watch and Glasses Co., Ltd. in the importation of watches, approached Defendant Gao Qingting to discuss smuggling watches directly from Hong Kong without customs declaration. Gao agreed. Subsequently, Li Yongjian twice air-shipped 575 watches of the Swiss brands Titoni, Omega, and Rado from Hong Kong into Jinan. Under the direction of Gao Qingting, Defendant Liu Guiliang, then Deputy Section Chief of the Supervision Section, knowing that the goods had not undergone any customs clearance procedures, nonetheless released them on both occasions. As determined by Jinan Customs, the value of these watches was RMB 1,774,746.24, and the evaded customs duties were RMB 763,494.80. After the case was uncovered, Jinan Customs seized 272 unsold watches, valued at RMB 962,903, from Jinan Hengdeli Watch and Glasses Co., Ltd.

In August 1996, Defendant Gao Qingting and Li Yongjian together visited Casio Langchao Communication Electronics Co., Ltd. Gao requested the company to cooperate with Li Yongjian in importing pager components. Li proposed to the company that the pager parts, which were originally imported from Japan to Qingdao and then sent to Jinan, could instead be shipped directly from Japan to Hong Kong, where he would be responsible for importing them into Jinan. The company objected on the grounds that this would increase freight costs. Li then suggested that during customs declaration, the complete sets of pager parts (tax rate 25%) could be falsely declared as integrated circuits (tax rate 6%) to reduce customs fees and offset the increased freight costs. Gao immediately agreed. From September 15 to December 6, 1996, Li Yongjian imported 47,200 complete sets of pager parts into the country in twelve shipments, falsely declared as integrated circuits. For the first shipment, Gao personally went to Jinan Airport to receive the goods. Under Gao's direction, Defendant Liu Guiliang also went to receive goods on three occasions to ensure smooth passage without inspection. As determined by Jinan Customs, the total value of these goods was RMB 19,867,110.30, and the evaded customs duties were RMB 3,019,800.90. After the case was uncovered, Jinan Customs seized 5,000 complete sets of pager parts; for the 42,200 sets that had entered production and sales and could not be seized, RMB 3,060,875 was recovered as proceeds.

The Jinan Intermediate People's Court held: During his tenure as Deputy Commissioner of Jinan Customs, Defendant Gao Qingting violated customs laws and regulations, colluded with others to smuggle goods, and the value of smuggled goods and the amount of evaded duties both exceeded the statutory thresholds for criminal offenses. The smuggled goods were in bulk quantities and intended for production and sales, not small quantities for daily use. Therefore, his conduct constituted the crime of smuggling ordinary goods. The charge by the prosecutorial authority of the crime of smuggling ordinary articles was inaccurate in nature. Article 4(1)(1) of the Supplementary Provisions Concerning the Punishment of Smuggling Crimes (hereinafter "Supplementary Provisions") adopted by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on January 21, 1988, provided: "Where the value of smuggled goods or articles is RMB 500,000 or more, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and shall also be fined not less than one time but not more than five times the value of the smuggled goods or articles, or have his property confiscated..." Article 12 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, effective October 1, 1997, provides: "If an act committed before the entry into force of this Law... was deemed a crime under the laws at the time, and if prosecution is to be pursued in accordance with the provisions of Section 8 of Chapter IV of the General Provisions, criminal liability shall be investigated under the laws at that time; however, if this Law does not deem it a crime or imposes a lighter punishment, this Law shall apply." Article 153(1)(1) of the Criminal Law provides: "Where the amount of evaded duties on smuggled goods or articles is RMB 500,000 or more, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and shall also be fined not less than one time but not more than five times the amount of evaded duties, or have his property confiscated..." Gao Qingting's conduct constituted a crime under both the Supplementary Provisions and the Criminal Law. In comparison, the Criminal Law bases sentencing on the amount of evaded duties, which is lighter than the Supplementary Provisions' sentencing based on the value of smuggled goods. Therefore, Gao Qingting's criminal conduct should be punished in accordance with Article 153(1)(1) of the Criminal Law. Additionally, in accordance with Article 57(1) of the Criminal Law, he shall also be sentenced to deprivation of political rights for life. As to the defense argument of Gao Qingting and his counsel that he did not participate in smuggling but merely connived at it: The court found that Gao Qingting's participation in smuggling was confirmed by his multiple confessions, the details of which were consistent with witness testimony, documentary evidence of customs declarations with false product descriptions, and physical evidence such as the smuggled watches and complete sets of pager parts seized by Jinan Customs. Gao personally went to the airport to receive smuggled goods for Li Yongjian. The evidence was conclusive and sufficient, and his defense and his counsel's arguments lacked factual basis and were not accepted. Defendant Liu Guiliang, as a customs officer, violated customs laws and regulations, engaged in favoritism and malpractice, and clearly knowing the conduct was smuggling, still allowed it to occur. The circumstances were serious. His conduct violated Article 411 of the Criminal Law. The prosecutorial authority's charge of the crime of conniving at smuggling was established. In view of the fact that Defendant Liu Guiliang committed the criminal acts under the direction of Gao Qingting, the defense counsel's request for a lighter punishment could be accepted. Accordingly, on September 9, 1998, the Jinan Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

Defendant Gao Qingting was convicted of the crime of smuggling ordinary goods and sentenced to life imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for life, and was also ordered to have confiscated his personal property consisting of RMB 2,250, two gold necklaces, and two gold rings; Defendant Liu Guiliang was convicted of the crime of conniving at smuggling and sentenced to three years' fixed-term imprisonment.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, Defendant Gao Qingting appealed to the Shandong High People's Court, reiterating his original defense arguments. His defense counsel requested a lighter or mitigated punishment on the grounds that Gao Qingting "had generally shown good conduct and had sincerely repented after the crime."

The Shandong High People's Court, after trial, held that the facts as found by the first instance regarding Appellant Gao Qingting and Defendant at First Instance Liu Guiliang were clear, and the evidence was conclusive and sufficient. Gao Qingting, as a customs officer, disregarded national interests, colluded with others to smuggle, evaded a huge amount of customs duties, and the circumstances were particularly serious. The criminal facts of Gao Qingting were confirmed by conclusive evidence and could not be denied. Gao Qingting's criminal conduct seriously undermined the national foreign trade control system and warranted severe punishment. His grounds of appeal were untenable. The defense counsel's opinion that he should be given a lighter or mitigated punishment lacked factual and legal basis and was not accepted. The first-instance judgment was correct in law and in the characterization of the crime, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. Accordingly, on November 19, 1998, the Shandong High People's Court, in accordance with Article 189(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following ruling:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.
